title: Canonical right-derived unit on an object in degree zero
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories with chosen derived categories and localization functors $Q_{\mathcal C},Q_{\mathcal D}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $\mathcal C$ has K-injective resolutions, and use the ordinary total right derived functor with its localization unit as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For an additive functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $M\in\mathcal C$, define the canonical morphism $u_F(M):F(M)[0]\to RF(M[0])$ to be $Q_{\mathcal D}$ of the inverse of the canonical single-complex comparison $F(M[0])\cong F(M)[0]$, followed by the localization unit of $RF$ on the homotopy class of $M[0]$. This is the specified composite, with no arbitrary choice of a morphism or an isomorphism and with no left-exactness or acyclicity assumption on $F$ or $M$.

source.place: Section 13.20, Tag 0156 (right derived functors and injective resolutions), localization-unit construction; unbounded K-injective convention of Tag 070K. The single-object composite is the construction recorded before lem-sbc-right-derived-single-zero-unit.
